I've attached a redlined version of the order form (high level edits only) and a usage summary so you can see the load pattern driving this. Can you confirm:
- whether Redwood can implement the tier migration effective 2027-07-01
- recommended proration approach for fees for the remainder of Q3
- any MSA cross-references we should be aware of (we were told there might be an implementation fee or minimums)

We'd like to get legal sign-off and a clean DocuSign route by the end of next week if possible. Copying our procurement lead Matt (matt.huang@medicorpx.com) for cadence.

Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: tiered rateband move + SOW edit for Q3 capacity

Laura — reviewed the customer redline and usage summary. High-level legal view and suggested language below. Attaching a marked-up order form (redline_orderform_jordan_v1.pdf).

1) MSA cross-checks:
- MSA Section 4.2 (Commitments & Adjustments): we permit Order Form amendments that adjust capacity but changes to committed capacity are subject to a fee proration model and a 30-day notice unless agreed otherwise.
- MSA Section 7.1 (Implementation & Acceptance): we can require an implementation window and acceptance testing if the integration touches private deployment components.

2) Suggested amendment language (short form):
"Effective July 1, 2027, Customer elects to reassign 40% of the committed throughput associated with SKU Tier B to SKU Tier A. Fees for the transition shall be prorated on a daily basis from the Effective Date to the end of the then-current billing period. Customer's billing for additional unit price differentials shall commence on the Effective Date. Redwood will schedule implementation activities and provide a mutually agreed acceptance window not to exceed 30 days."

3) Fees/proration: recommend daily proration for Q3; if customer prefers month-level proration, we can accept but require a billing true-up invoice. Operationally, if we cannot complete implementation by 2027-07-01, billing should start on the earlier of (i) completed implementation date or (ii) 2027-07-15 (we set fallback to avoid revenue leakage). Please let me know which fallback you prefer.

4) Implementation fee: given the scale (40% reassignment) propose a one-time implementation fee of $6,500 to cover scheduling/validation. If sales wants to waive, flag it for approval from Revenue Ops.

Next steps: Laura, if you approve, I'll convert these changes into clean amendment language and an Order Form exhibit. Naomi/Connor, confirm ops timeline and earliest realistic Go-Live.

-Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts — Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com

Samantha / Matt — thanks for the clear ask and for the usage file. Quick summary and proposed next steps:

2) Ops (Naomi/Connor) — Naomi has confirmed they can schedule the work but requests a firm Go-Live window to be confirmed no later than 2027-06-15. If we receive customer sign-off and the signed amendment by 2027-06-20 we can meet a July 1 effective date; otherwise billing fallback will be 07/15 as Jordan proposed.

3) Proposed path: Jordan will convert the redline into a clean amendment; I will send a DocuSign envelope with: (a) Amendment to Order Form (clean), (b) Revised Exhibit A (line items), (c) Updated SOW paragraph for integration window. Please review and confirm by 2027-03-15.
